clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country to buy an apple orchard in March 1952, within the year: June wrote to her sister Edna every day and withdrew to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter stayed out in the trees and clashed with June over money for new trees; Glen fought at school and was sent home twice; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan in May 1968, within the year: Walter drank heavily and clashed with Glen over who was to blame; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks grew worse that winter; Nora began wetting the bed again; Ida's heart trouble was found and she stopped working. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours and fought with Marian every night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating and lost a lot of weight; Nora kept to her room and said little to her mother; Walter drank again after six years off it. By June 1976, Nora was eating again and made the track team.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990, within the year: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Hollis rowed most nights. By August 1991, Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, after Wilma took a flat in town in June.

periods.words: The one that stands out is the year Dad lost his job, when I was 14.

declined.reason: 1994: an acute episode. The wildfire arrived on 12 August 1994, the family was ordered out and slept three nights in the school gym, and all shifts—Nora's anxiety, Lily's nausea, the conflict between Nora and Hollis, Owen's need for light—fell within those same few days and the immediately following days. The family was allowed home on 15 August, Nora was calm again once home, and the children were back at school that week. The whole span settles within days of the start, marking an acute episode around a real threat, not a period.
